slides.texte_overlay:
How to negotiate your rent
without being pushy
Be the tenant they don't want to lose. Pay on time, report problems early, keep the place clean. Good tenants have real leverage, because finding a new one costs the owner money.
Check what similar places really cost. Look at a few listings in your area before you talk. "Flats like this one are going for a bit less now" is a fair point, not a threat.
Ask before the renewal, not after. Two or three months ahead, in a friendly message or call. Early conversations feel like planning together, not like a last-minute fight.
Offer something in return. A longer lease, small repairs you handle yourself, flexibility on dates. Giving the owner security often matters more to them than a few extra euros.
Put your request in one clear sentence. "Would you consider keeping the rent the same if I sign for two years?" Short, polite and specific is far easier to say yes to.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A calmer, sharper head makes money conversations with your landlord feel normal instead of terrifying.

slides.texte_overlay: Get any agreement in writing. A short email confirming the new rent and dates protects you both. Friendly deals are great, and written friendly deals are even better.
